'''Grace Mary Flickinger''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament|SBS]]}} (September 7, 1935 – June 11, 2024) was an American religious sister and college professor. She was a biology professor at [[Xavier University of Louisiana]] (XULA) from 1968 to 2016, and served as the school's faculty athletics representative from 1981 to 2016.

==Early life and education==
Flickinger was born in the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]] and raised in [[Millville, New Jersey]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=1948-06-14 |title=Graduate 20 at St. Mary's School |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-millville-daily-graduate-20-at-st-m/160713871/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=The Millville Daily |pages=1 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> the youngest child of Edmond J. B. Flickinger and Helen C. Reardon Flickinger.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=1977-02-17 |title=Former Millville Resident Doing Research; Nun Says Palm Prints Help Diagnose Disease |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/vineland-times-journal-former-millville/160717400/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=Vineland Times Journal |pages=8 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her mother was a nurse, and her father was a glassworker and veteran of [[World War I]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1984-01-30 |title=Obituary for Edmond J. Flickinger |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-of-cumberland-county-obituary-f/160715986/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=The News of Cumberland County |via=Newspapers.com|pages=4}}</ref> She graduated from [[Sacred Heart High School (New Jersey)|Sacred Heart High School]] in 1952.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1952-06-04 |title=Vineland Catholic High Graduates 46 at Ceremony |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/press-of-atlantic-city-vineland-catholic/160715095/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=Press of Atlantic City |pages=3 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She attended Blessed Sacrament College, and earned a master's degree from [[Catholic University of America]]. She completed doctoral studies at the [[University of Southern Mississippi]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=1989-04-25 |title=Appreciation banquet scheduled at N.C. A&T |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/news-and-record-appreciation-banquet-sch/160716821/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=News and Record |pages=43 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

Flickinger joined the [[Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament]] in 1952, and professed her final vows in 1960. 

==Career==
Flickinger was a biology professor as Xavier University of Louisiana from 1968 to 2016,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xavier University of Louisiana Mourns The Passing of Sr. Grace Mary Flickinger, SBS |url=https://www.xula.edu/news/2024/06/xavier-university-of-louisiana-mourns-the-passing-of-sr-grace-mary-flickinger.html |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=Xavier University of Louisiana}}</ref> and was active in the school's athletic programs, and in sports administration at the conference level. She was president of the [[HBCU Athletic Conference|Gulf Coast Athletic Conference]] (GCAC) twice, from 1990 to 1991, and from 1995 to 1999. She was academic advisor to the XULA basketball team, and founded the Academic Coordination of Athletes program at XULA in 1981.<ref name=":1" /> She took particular interest in preparing the school's students for admission to medical schools.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McConnaughey |first=Janet |date=1996-10-06 |title=Tough-love theory becomes a science at small college |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/evansville-press-tough-love-theory-becom/160716575/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=Evansville Press |pages=15 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Yardley |first=Jim |date=1994-09-13 |title=Xavier is No. 1 i placing blacks in medical school |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-constitution-xavier-is-no-1/160717946/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |work=The Atlanta Constitution |pages=3 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

Flickinger was inducted into the [[NAIA independent schools|NAIA]] Hall of Fame in 1998. She received NAIA's Wally Schwartz Award in 2007. She was inducted into the XULA Hall of Fame in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sister Grace Mary Flickinger (2022) - Hall of Fame |url=https://xulagold.com/honors/hall-of-fame/sister-grace-mary-flickinger/7 |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=Xavier University of Louisiana Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

Flickinger's area of research was [[dermatoglyphics]], or the characteristics of fingerprints and palm prints, especially as indicators of health or genetic conditions.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Flickinger Sr. |first1=Grace Mary |last2=Yarbrough |first2=Karen M. |date=1976 |title=Dermatoglyphics of Apache and Navajo Indians |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ajpa.1330450115 |journal=American Journal of Physical Anthropology |language=en |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=117–121 |doi=10.1002/ajpa.1330450115 |bibcode=1976AJPA...45..117F |issn=1096-8644|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
==Publications==
* "Dermatoglyphics of Apache and Navajo Indians" (1976, with Karen M. Yarbrough)
* "Let a Slinky Do Your Teaching!" (1978)<ref>Flickinger, Grace Mary. "Let a Slinky Do Your Teaching!" ''Journal of College Science Teaching'' (1978): 332-332.</ref>
==Personal life==
Flickinger retired to her order's [[Motherhouse|mother house]] in Pennsylvania.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2017-11-21 |title=Homecoming was a banner day for Sister Grace Mary |url=https://xulagold.com/news/2017/11/21/gen-flickinger-banner.aspx |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=Xavier University of Louisiana Athletics |language=en}}</ref> She died in 2024, at the age of 88, in Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-11 |title=XULA icon Sister Grace Mary Flickinger dies at age 88 |url=https://xulagold.com/news/2024/6/11/gen-flickinger-obit.aspx |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=Xavier University of Louisiana Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Connor |first=Shay |date=2024-06-12 |title=Sister Grace Mary Flickinger, longtime Xavier University educator, dead at 88 |url=https://www.wdsu.com/article/new-orleans-grace-mary-flickinger-dead/61086887 |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=WDSU |language=en}}</ref> A banner honoring Flickinger is displayed in the rafters at XULA's Convocation Center.<ref name=":2" />
